# Jubilees Chapter 48 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Exodus; Mastema and Moses; the plagues; the crossing of the sea

---

**48:1** And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee, thou didst go in to the inner part of the dwelling of Pharaoh. And the LORD sent the plagues upon Pharaoh and upon his household, for Pharaoh would not hearken to the command of Moses.

**48:2** And the LORD sent all these plagues upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt: blood and frogs and lice and flies and murrain and boils and hail and locusts and darkness and the death of the firstborn.

**48:3** And the LORD executed his judgments on all their gods; and he burnt their idols and smote their firstborn.

**48:4** And everything was broken before Moses, and the LORD brought out his people Israel from Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with great terror and signs and wonders.

**48:5** And Mastema stood before the LORD, and he strengthened the hearts of the Egyptians and made them hard, and he urged them to pursue after Israel.

**48:6** And the LORD our God said to him: "Leave them." And he went with the Egyptians.

**48:7** And Moses went down to the sea, and the LORD split the sea before him and before all Israel.

**48:8** And the spirit of Mastema came upon Pharaoh and caused him to pursue after Israel with his army and his chariots into the sea.

**48:9** And the LORD our God dried up the sea, and the waters went before Israel as a wall, both on the right hand and on the left.

**48:10** And the waters closed upon the Egyptians and their army and all the hosts of Pharaoh who were pursuing Israel into the sea, and they were all drowned.

**48:11** And the LORD saved Israel from the hand of Egypt on that day, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.

**48:12** And Israel feared the LORD greatly and they believed in Moses and in the LORD, and he was praised and glorified.

**48:13** And Mastema was bound and imprisoned behind the children of Israel, so that he should not accuse them.

**48:14** And the LORD our God was with them in the pillar of fire by night and in the pillar of cloud by day; and he went before them, guiding them on their way.

**48:15** And they came to the Wilderness of Sin on the fifteenth day of the second month after the exodus from the land of Egypt.

**48:16** And the people murmured against Moses because there was no bread or water, and they said: "It were better for us to die in Egypt than to die in this wilderness."

**48:17** And Moses went up to the LORD, and the LORD said to him: "I will give them flesh to eat and bread from heaven." And Moses descended and spoke all things to the children of Israel.

**48:18** And Moses stretched out his staff, and manna rained down from heaven, and they ate it.

**48:19** And the LORD said to Moses: "Gather of it each man for his eating, and gather not on the Sabbath." And Moses spoke to the people.

---

*EMET notes: Chapter 48 is the Jubilees Exodus narrative. Its most distinctive feature is the explicit role of Mastema: he "strengthened the hearts of the Egyptians" (v.5) — in Jubilees, the hardening of Pharaoh's heart is attributed to Mastema rather than directly to God (contrast Exodus 4-14). This is a significant theological move to absolve God of directly causing Pharaoh's stubbornness. The binding of Mastema (v.13) after the Red Sea is unique to Jubilees.*
